input.quote: (a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials
input.rationale:
No sole-supplier or requirements-purchase obligation is imposed on us. Article IX frames supply entirely as our option: Section 9.4(a) (p0508) gives Ono "the right (but not the obligation)" to Manufacture or engage its own Subcontractor, with a Know-How transfer/step-in right, and Section 9.4(b) (p0509) says Ono "shall have the right to obtain from Array" its commercial requirements, with a Supply Agreement entered into only "Upon Ono's request". Section 9.1(a) (p0495) obliges Array to supply or secure supply of our requirements with no reciprocal commitment by us to buy exclusively from Array, and Section 9.5 (p0516) passes through the benefit of Array's Third Party supplier arrangements. Our freedom to second-source is therefore fully preserved, meeting the preferred position. The only exclusivity binding us is Section 8.2 (p0491), which is a reciprocal field non-compete rather than exclusive dealing: it is mutual (Array and its Controlled Affiliates are equally bound), limited to two defined Competing Product categories, limited to the Ono Territory, time-limited to a defined date, and is the quid pro quo for the exclusive licences granted to us under Sections 2.1(a) and 2.1(c) (p0162, p0164), which benefit us and are not flagged. That covenant sits at or above the fallback; we note only that it does not expressly release us from the restriction if Array itself commercialises a Competing Product (it instead ends the royalty period), a minor sub-element rather than a material failure. No redline proposed.</rationale>
